analysis:
Examined provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/ProviderLoop.swift base text (lines 1-1125) against the supplied change map. The visible head changes are: (1) autopilotHistory tuple at line 343 gains labels plus an extra `detail: String?` field; (2) new in-memory state declared at head lines 356-404 for Autopilot placement and download (autopilotAdoptedModelIDs, autopilotHolds, autopilotDownloadSettingsOverride, autopilotDownloadStorage, and an autopilot download coordinator). The patch excerpt is truncated at the autopilotDownloadCoo... member, and the head text itself was not supplied, only the base. These are stored-property declarations; no new network, crypto, authorization or file-handling code is visible in this file. The behavior behind them lives in companion files (ProviderLoop+AutopilotPlacement, ProviderLoop+AutopilotDownload) that were not supplied.

No concrete regression can be cited here. Security-relevant integration questions for the next pass: (a) the new Autopilot download coordinator is described as downloading models on the operator's behalf, with verified builds joining the Autopilot set rather than the advertised set. The companion files must be checked for weight-hash verification before a model is adopted or served (T-012, T-027, A-004), and for whether downloads that bypass the advertised-set guard can be loaded and served unverified. (b) The new `detail` string stored in autopilotHistory should be checked for whether it can carry prompt content or sensitive paths into the daemon state file or coordinator messages (A-001, T-058). (c) autopilotAdoptedModelIDs and autopilotHolds should be checked for whether they bypass the retiringModels and failedSelfTestHashes fail-closed tombstones. (d) The download-settings override read from the config file should be checked for tamper or path-trust handling, which is relevant to TB-003. The prefix-cache threat T-041 is unaffected by the visible changes in this file. Coverage is limited to base text plus a truncated patch, so this is an orientation-level review rather than a verdict on the full PR.
